Operator: Good day, and welcome to the CyberShield Technologies Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss CyberShield Technologies' results for the Q3. With me on today's call are Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez.

Dr. Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us. CyberShield Technologies had a strong Q3, driven by continued demand for our cybersecurity solutions and our commitment to innovation. We are seeing increased adoption of our Nexus platform, which is helping organizations better protect themselves against increasingly sophisticated cyber threats.

Our focus remains on four key areas: driving low churn through superior retention and expansions, growing our cohort of high-value customers with over $100K in ARR, accelerating platform adoption ahead of point solutions, and delivering impactful new product and feature launches that address emerging risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Elena. As Elena mentioned, we had a strong Q3. Revenue for the quarter was $350 million, representing a 28% increase year-over-year. This growth was driven by strong performance across all of our product lines. Our gross margin was 78%, and our operating expenses were $220 million. Net income for the quarter was $85 million, or $0.92 per share.

Turning to our customer metrics, let's start with churn rate and the drivers behind it, which provide a clear view into the stickiness of our platform in this demanding cybersecurity environment. Our model is largely SaaS-driven, with more than 85% of our ARR coming from multi-year contracts covering our integrated Endpoint Detection and Response, Secure Access Service Edge, and Cloud Workload Protection Platform offerings.

On the numbers, our gross dollar churn rate was 4.2% for Q3, a 90 basis point improvement year-over-year and our 11th consecutive quarter of progress. Annualized, that's about 16.8%, significantly undercutting the industry benchmarks of 20-25% from reports like Bessemer Venture Partners' Cloud Index and KeyBanc's SaaS studies. Compared to peers such as CrowdStrike and SentinelOne, who've reported 5-7% quarterly gross churn recently, our platform strategy has given us an edge.

Digging deeper, net revenue retention climbed to 118% in Q3, up from 112% last year. This captures solid expansions, with an average 1.25x net expansion per account, powered by upsells to our AI-enhanced Next-Gen SIEM and Zero Trust Network Access capabilities. We generated $42 million in expansion ARR, more than covering the $28 million from downsells and churn.

By segment: Enterprises with 500+ employees, which make up 65% of ARR, saw 3.1% churn—zero among our top 50 customers—with expansions at 22% tied to multi-year renewals averaging 3.2 years. Mid-market, 100-500 employees and 25% of ARR, had 6.8% churn, better than 8.2% YoY, thanks to targeted customer success teams. SMBs under 100 employees, 10% of ARR, hit 9.5%, as expected for that group, but we've improved 200 basis points with self-serve onboarding.

Reasons for churn, based on Customer Success analysis and NPS data: Voluntary churn was 68% of losses, $19 million ARR, while involuntary like non-payment or M&A was 32%, $9 million. Top voluntary factor at 35% was budget shifts—IT fatigue from inflation and recession concerns led some mid-market firms to consolidate, like one $2.5 million ARR loss to Palo Alto's Prisma. Our Q1 'CyberShield One' bundle cut this by 40% YoY with 20-30% savings on EDR+SASE stacks over point buys.

Competitive losses were 25%, mainly to hyperscaler tools like Microsoft Defender or Zscaler's ZTNA, with two EMEA firms noting quicker AWS setups. Our HyperShield Alliance with AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud boosted win rates 15% and recaptured one account.

Product gaps or incidents drove 18%, three customers totaling $4 million ARR citing ransomware rollback issues despite our 7-minute MTTR via AI detection. We've launched ShieldAI Recover in beta, a decryption tool averting $150 million in losses for testers, nearly eliminating this churn.

M&A and contract ends took 22%, 12 deals, similar to last year's Thoma Bravo activity.

Regionally: North America, 72% of ARR, at 3.5% churn, helped by CCPA and financial services SEC rules with 28% expansions. EMEA, 18%, 5.1% churn amid GDPR pauses but NIS2 gains added €15 million ARR in telco CWPP for OT. APAC, 10%, 7.2% from yen issues and Trend Micro rivalry, but 35% NRR in Japan/Korea via PDPA modules.

We've put $50 million into FY24 priorities: Customer Success 2.0 with CSMs for 90% of $1M+ accounts and QBRs boosting renewals 25%; GenAI threat hunting like Falcon EDR at 92% zero-day flags per MITRE; and ML churn prediction with 75% saves. Q4 guide: 4.0% gross churn or lower, NRR 115%+, supporting FY25 ARR of $1.2 billion, up 28%, as our 99.8% breach prevention shines amid 37% ransomware rise per Chainalysis.

Next, a leading indicator of our momentum: customers with over $100K ARR. We closed Q3 with 528 such accounts, up 17% year-over-year from 451 and 8% sequentially from 489 in Q2. They represent 42% of total ARR, versus 38% last year, with average ARR per at $245K, a 12% rise from upsells to Autonomous Threat Response and SIEM ties like Splunk and Elastic.

New logos: 62 net adds, beating targets by 15%, including a Fortune 100 bank on CNAPP for AWS/Azure after Clop MOVEit exploits, plus healthcare and manufacturing under NIST 800-53 and EU DORA.

NRR for this group was 128%, with 40% expanding via AI analytics usage pricing. 'Forge Elite' partnerships with CrowdStrike and Palo Alto sped deployments, 22% XDR attach.

North America: 380 customers, 72%, +10% sequential on MGM and Change Healthcare breaches. EMEA: 92, +25% YoY on GDPR/NIS2, telcos/energy. APAC: 56, +30% YoY, Tencent wins in Japan/Australia against Lazarus APTs.

This validates platform bets as Gartner sees $215 billion cyber spend in 2025, XDR/zero-trust at 25% CAGR. Q4 GenAI deception grids cut MTTD 40%. We eye 600 by FY24 end, $1.2 billion pipeline, 35% multi-year, with <2% churn de-risking us versus Zscaler or SentinelOne.

Shifting to platform adoption versus point products—a key sign of the market moving from siloed tools like standalone EDR or firewalls to our Nexus unified XDR, SASE, CSPM, and identity detection via AI orchestration.

In Q3, 75% of new logos chose full Nexus, up from 62% YoY and 45% two years back—11 quarters running. Point-only deals under 15% of new ACV, down from 28%. Platform ARR at $1.2 billion, +58% YoY; points $285 million, +12%. IDC sees platforms at 65% new spend by 2025 amid $4.45 million breach costs per IBM.

Customers hate 45-tool sprawl per Gartner, 277-day MTTR per Ponemon. Nexus cuts to <30 days with 10 trillion daily events, Nexus Copilot for hunting/SOAR. Nexus Fabric API integrates ServiceNow, Splunk, Okta zero-touch.

North America: 82% adoption, 52% bookings, Fortune 500s swap Symantec/Check Point for 40% OpEx cuts, NRR 128% vs 108% points. EMEA: 71%, +15 points, EU Sovereignty Vault wins DAX banks from McAfee. APAC: 68%, +22 points, zero-trust SASE vs Zscaler; Nexus Lite pilots for China.

$250 million R&D for Nexus Horizon CWPP, 20% ACV boost. Microsoft/AWS co-sell at $100 million run rate. Platform churn <2%, 35% expansions. Guide: 80% adoption, $1.7 billion platform ARR FY24, +20 gross margin points, outpacing SentinelOne/Fortinet in $200 billion TAM.

Finally, our recent launches fueling this growth, responding to 42% AI-phishing rise and 35% ransomware per our lab/Chainalysis.

Flagship: ShieldXDR Pro GA March, endpoint/network/cloud/identity AI pane with NeuroThreat Engine on 15PB data, 98.7% zero-days via graph networks for multi-cloud. $180 million ARR in three months, 15% Q3 bookings; Fortune 50 from Defender, 40% faster MTTR; 125% NRR, auto-quarantine 85%. Gartner Leader, +12 vision.

SecureEdge SASE 3.0 RSA April: SD-WAN/ZTNA/CASB/DLP, 99.999% uptime 250 PoPs, Adaptive Risk with UEBA/Mandiant intel, post-quantum Kyber. 22% mid-market share Frost, $95 million ARR +160% YoY, 60% Zscaler rips for 30% TCO; <2% churn.

EndpointShield Elite: RansomVault Recovery air-gapped backups, 65% faster post-Clop, +18% seats $45 million ARR.

IDShield: Passwordless FIDO2 for OT/IoT amid 50% ICS attacks Dragos, 110% identity expansion, auto OEM vs Conti.

Regions: NA 62% $200 million CISA/SEC; EMEA +45% $110 million GDPR €2.7B fines, 35% DACH; APAC +75% $75 million Singapore/Japan NTT; LATAM +30% Brazil Pix.

$250 million R&D, 22% revenue, 17 ML patents. Beat Cortex XDR cloud perf G2 4.8/5, 20% cheaper. AWS $50 million pipeline. Q4: QuantumShield HSM, GenAI copilot; 30-35% bookings, $4.8 billion ARR FYE in $215 billion 13.5% CAGR TAM.

We are confident that we are well-positioned to continue to drive growth and profitability in the years to come.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: [Instructions for Q&A session]. First question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith: Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Michael, on churn—you called out some improvements in mid-market and SMB, but with macro pressures, how confident are you in the Q4 guide below 4%, and any color on competitive dynamics?

Michael Chen: Thanks, Ben. We're very confident in sub-4% Q4 gross churn. The investments in Customer Success 2.0, GenAI hunting, and churn prediction are delivering—75% save rates—and our platform efficacy with 99.8% prevention is resonating as ransomware climbs. Competitively, HyperShield Alliance is flipping losses, like that EMEA recapture, and bundles are shielding against Prisma shifts. Regional tailwinds like NIS2 and SEC rules bolster this.

Operator: Next question comes from Sarah Lee with Morgan Stanley.

Sarah Lee: Great results. Elena or Michael, with NRR at 118% and expansions strong, how does the $100K+ cohort growth factor into FY25 ARR guide, and any updates there?

Dr. Elena Vasquez: Sarah, thanks. The 528 $100K+ customers, up 17% YoY, are core to our $1.2 billion FY25 ARR outlook, up 28%. Their 128% NRR, low churn under 2%, and pipeline of $1.2 billion opportunities—35% multi-year—de-risk the model. Land-and-expand in XDR to SASE, plus hyperscaler partnerships, positions us to hit 600 by FY24 end.

Operator: Next question comes from Tom Rivera with JPMorgan.

Tom Rivera: Raj, impressive on launches like ShieldXDR Pro and SecureEdge. With platform adoption at 75%, what's the CTO view on integrating these with Nexus Horizon CWPP, and roadmap for agentless tech?

Dr. Raj Patel: Tom, Nexus Horizon builds directly on ShieldXDR and SecureEdge, previewed Q3 with runtime CWPP unifying Prisma-like features agentless. NeuroThreat and Adaptive Risk fuse seamlessly for 40% faster MTTD, post-quantum ready. Q4 QuantumShield and GenAI copilot enable natural language hunting. R&D at $250 million ensures we lead in AI/zero-trust convergence, outpacing peers in multi-cloud per MITRE/G2.

Operator: Next question comes from Lisa Chen with Barclays.

Lisa Chen: Solid metrics across the board. Michael, platform ARR $1.2 billion at 58% growth versus points—how do you see that mix shifting into FY25, and impact on margins?

Michael Chen: Lisa, thanks. Platform mix to 80% adoption by year-end drives $1.7 billion FY24 platform ARR, adding 20 margin points from efficiencies. FY25 accelerates as tool sprawl fades—NRR 128% platforms vs 108% points, churn sub-2% vs 8%. Nexus Fabric and co-sells with Microsoft/AWS scale this, capturing share in $200 billion TAM against point-focused competitors.

Operator: That concludes today's Q&A.

Dr. Elena Vasquez: Thank you, everyone, for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees, customers, and partners for their continued support. We are excited about the opportunities ahead and are confident that we can continue to deliver strong results.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
